body:
# Reading Yánluó the way it was meant to be written
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Yánluó** is what the evidence put back.

Yánluó's mythology is procedural: not adventures but cases. His stories are judgments — and the judgments are always, the texts insist, simply the soul's own deeds read back to it. Before he was a king of hell he was the first man to die: the Ṛgveda's Yama chose mortality, found the road to the other world, and became the guide and host of the fathers — honoured with songs and offerings.  Buddhism inherited him as the dharma-king who interrogates the dead: the three messengers — old age, sickness, death — are his summonses, sent to every house.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Yánluó
- **ASCII form:** yanluo
- **Meaning:** "'King Yan' (閻羅, from Yama), the judge of the dead"
- **Domain of influence:** Judgment, Underworld, Order
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 269 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Yánluó** to *yanluo* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **a → á** — Stress mark (acute/tone): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ó** — Stress mark (acute/tone): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Yánluó** lives at [/sites/yanluo/](/sites/yanluo/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/yanluo/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/yanluo/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/yanluo/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Yánluó** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — The judge of the dead, enthroned in his courtroom with the record books of every life — wealth and rank are nothing before him.
- **Insurance & Protection Services** — The exact record and the final accounting; judgment as audit.
- **Software, Cloud & Developer Infrastructure** — The immutable ledger of deeds; the audit log made sacred.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/yanluo/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
